subject: Architecture
title: Timber Skyscrapers: Wood Goes Tall
description: One-minute skill: Timber Skyscrapers: Wood Goes Tall.

hook.text: Engineers are now building skyscrapers from wood. Not log cabins — precision-engineered timber towers.

buildup.text: Cross-laminated timber is layered and glued into panels rivaling concrete in strength and rigidity.

discovery.text: Ascent in Milwaukee stands 25 stories — the world's tallest hybrid mass timber building.

twist.text: Timber construction is 25% faster than concrete because prefabricated panels snap together on site.

climax.text: Japan plans W350, an 1,148-foot timber tower for Tokyo — a wooden skyscraper taller than the Eiffel Tower.

punchline.text: Steel and concrete dominated a century. Wood might dominate the next.

quiz.question: How much faster is mass timber construction compared to concrete?
